headline: Bonds up to $900,000 for a 14 Mulberry Street resource center, and an elderly and disabled tax exemption income limit increase.
summary: Aldermen will consider two ordinances, including a change to elderly and disabled tax exemption income limits. Other items include a resolution opposing an ICE Detention Center in Merrimack and a Harbor Homes housing agreement change.
items: Assessing Department communication on increasing the elderly and disabled income limits
Calling special meetings on November 10, 2026 for the paving program and November 24, 2026 for school finances
Public comment on items expected to be acted on tonight
Mayor's request to approve a Ford F250 pick-up truck
Confirmation of Dalia Ragas as Deputy Treasurer/Tax Collector
Confirmation of re-appointments of Lisa Tourangeau and Jennifer Bishop to the Citizens Advisory Commission
Ordinance O-26-025 increasing the elderly and disabled tax exemption maximum income amounts, with committee recommendation for final passage
Ordinance O-26-026 on approvals for gasoline, electricity, and natural gas contracts and purchasing extensions or renewals, with committee recommendation for final passage
Resolution R-26-015 supporting the Town of Merrimack in its opposition to an ICE Detention Center, tabled at the February 24, 2026 meeting
Resolution R-26-020 authorizing bonds not to exceed $900,000 for a resource center at 14 Mulberry Street, tabled at the April 22, 2026 special meeting
Resolution R-26-080 authorizing an amendment to Section 7 of the Harbor Homes CDBG agreement for transitional and permanent housing for non-veterans and their families
